title: 415. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Reference Angle Reduction
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Sine of a Quadrant II angle
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a sine by reducing to a reference angle and attaching the correct sign.
questions.question: Using a reference angle, what is the exact value of \(\sin 150^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: The reference angle of \(150^\circ\) is \(180^\circ-150^\circ=30^\circ\). The angle is in Quadrant II, where sine is positive. Therefore \(\sin 150^\circ=+\sin 30^\circ=\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.hint: Find the reference angle, then decide the sign from the quadrant.

questions.concept: Cosine of a Quadrant II angle
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a cosine by reducing to a reference angle and attaching the correct sign.
questions.question: Using a reference angle, what is the exact value of \(\cos 120^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: The reference angle of \(120^\circ\) is \(180^\circ-120^\circ=60^\circ\). The angle is in Quadrant II, where cosine is negative. Therefore \(\cos 120^\circ=-\cos 60^\circ=-\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.hint: The reference angle gives the size; the quadrant gives the sign.

questions.concept: Tangent of a Quadrant III angle
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a tangent by reducing to a reference angle.
questions.question: Using a reference angle, what is the exact value of \(\tan 225^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: The reference angle of \(225^\circ\) is \(225^\circ-180^\circ=45^\circ\). The angle is in Quadrant III, where sine and cosine are both negative, so tangent is positive. Therefore \(\tan 225^\circ=+\tan 45^\circ=1\).
questions.hint: In Quadrant III both sine and cosine are negative; consider the sign of their quotient.

questions.concept: Sine of a Quadrant IV angle
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a sine in Quadrant IV by reducing to a reference angle.
questions.question: Using a reference angle, what is the exact value of \(\sin 300^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: The reference angle of \(300^\circ\) is \(360^\circ-300^\circ=60^\circ\). The angle is in Quadrant IV, where sine is negative. Therefore \(\sin 300^\circ=-\sin 60^\circ=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\). The value \(-\frac{1}{2}\) would correspond to a reference angle of \(30^\circ\).
questions.hint: Subtract the angle from \(360^\circ\) to obtain the reference angle.

questions.concept: Cosine of a radian angle in Quadrant III
questions.learningObjective: Reduce a radian angle to its reference angle to evaluate a cosine.
questions.question: Using a reference angle, what is the exact value of \(\cos\frac{7\pi}{6}\)?
questions.explanation: The reference angle is \(\frac{7\pi}{6}-\pi=\frac{\pi}{6}\). The angle is in Quadrant III, where cosine is negative. Therefore \(\cos\frac{7\pi}{6}=-\cos\frac{\pi}{6}=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\). The value \(-\frac{1}{2}\) is \(\sin\frac{7\pi}{6}\).
questions.hint: Subtract \(\pi\) to find the reference angle, and keep the same function.

questions.concept: Rewriting a sine with an acute angle
questions.learningObjective: Express the sine of a Quadrant III angle as a signed sine of an acute angle.
questions.question: Which expression equals \(\sin 200^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: The reference angle of \(200^\circ\) is \(200^\circ-180^\circ=20^\circ\). The angle is in Quadrant III, where sine is negative. Therefore \(\sin 200^\circ=-\sin 20^\circ\approx -0.342\).
questions.hint: The reduction keeps the function and the reference angle; only the sign must be decided.

questions.concept: Rewriting a cosine with an acute angle
questions.learningObjective: Express the cosine of a Quadrant IV angle as a signed cosine of an acute angle.
questions.question: Which expression equals \(\cos 340^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: The reference angle of \(340^\circ\) is \(360^\circ-340^\circ=20^\circ\). The angle is in Quadrant IV, where the \(x\)-coordinate, and hence cosine, is positive. Therefore \(\cos 340^\circ=+\cos 20^\circ\approx 0.940\).
questions.hint: Decide whether the \(x\)-coordinate is positive or negative in the quadrant of the angle.

questions.concept: Tangent of a Quadrant II angle
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a tangent in Quadrant II by reducing to a reference angle.
questions.question: Using a reference angle, what is the exact value of \(\tan 150^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: The reference angle of \(150^\circ\) is \(30^\circ\). In Quadrant II sine is positive and cosine is negative, so tangent is negative. Therefore \(\tan 150^\circ=-\tan 30^\circ=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\). The value \(-\sqrt{3}\) is \(\tan 120^\circ\), whose reference angle is \(60^\circ\).
questions.hint: The reference angle is measured to the \(x\)-axis, so it is \(180^\circ\) minus the angle.

questions.concept: Sine of an angle beyond several turns
questions.learningObjective: Reduce a large angle by full turns before using a reference angle.
questions.question: What is the exact value of \(\sin 1110^\circ\)?
questions.explanation: Remove full turns: \(1110^\circ-3\cdot 360^\circ=1110^\circ-1080^\circ=30^\circ\). Hence \(\sin 1110^\circ=\sin 30^\circ=\frac{1}{2}\). The value \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) is \(\sin 60^\circ\), which would arise from an error in the subtraction.
questions.hint: Subtract multiples of \(360^\circ\) until the angle is between \(0^\circ\) and \(360^\circ\).

questions.concept: Cosine of a large negative radian angle
questions.learningObjective: Combine coterminal reduction with a reference angle for a negative radian measure.
questions.question: What is the exact value of \(\cos\left(-\frac{19\pi}{3}\right)\)?
questions.explanation: Add four full turns: \(-\frac{19\pi}{3}+8\pi=-\frac{19\pi}{3}+\frac{24\pi}{3}=\frac{5\pi}{3}\). This angle is in Quadrant IV with reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\), and cosine is positive there. Therefore the value is \(\cos\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.hint: Add multiples of \(2\pi\) to reach an angle between \(0\) and \(2\pi\), then use the quadrant to fix the sign.
